logline: A respected family doctor discovers her husband's years-long affair and methodically dismantles his life - only to find that revenge reshapes her own identity just as violently.

renewal.note: Single-season limited run; concluded May 16, 2020 at 16 episodes. No continuation announced. The series was adapted from the BBC One drama Doctor Foster.

bollymeter.basis: Historic cable ratings peak at 28.371% finale viewership - the highest in Korean cable television history at broadcast. Critics and Baeksang Arts Award voters aligned on Kim Hee-ae's performance and the screenplay's psychological ferocity.

pull_quotes.text: Bold in its attempts to tackle a controversial subject; offers a rare representation of a strong female lead.

seasons.review_body: Adapted from the BBC drama Doctor Foster, this 16-episode revenge thriller became the highest-rated cable drama in Korean television history, with its finale pulling a 28.371% nationwide rating and surpassing the previous record held by Sky Castle. Critics praised the screenplay's psychological precision and Kim Hee-ae's formidable lead performance, with the 56th Baeksang Arts Awards granting her Best Actress and director Mo Wan-il Best Director. The series earned controversy for its unflinching portrayal of infidelity and violence, but reviewers noted that the 19+ rating reflects a willingness to portray the dark mechanics of a marriage's collapse with rare realism. The show operates as a sustained study in power, vengeance, and the cost of winning.

episode_reviews.title: Infidelity
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes Dr Ji Sun-woo as a composed, admired figure in her community before quietly assembling the evidence of her husband's betrayal. The restraint in these early scenes makes the emotional detonation land harder - the show signals early that it will trust the audience with ambiguity.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The discovery that confirms Sun-woo's suspicions - the series earns its reputation for psychological voltage from the first hour.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale drew the historic 28.371% cable rating as it delivered on the series' central moral question: whether a woman who wins her revenge is truly free. The resolution is deliberately unsentimental, refusing the clean resolution that genre convention would allow.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The scene between Sun-woo and her son that closes the series - the cost of the preceding sixteen episodes fully visible in a single exchange.
